title: Trail for Healing the Burn: An Interpretive Network Supporting Post-Fire Recovery

awards.name: WLA Awards
awards.distinction: Award of Excellence — Concept – Analysis & Planning

summary: A trail network in Plumas County connects forest restoration with public learning, making the changing landscapes of post-fire recovery accessible over time.
description: Following the Dixie Fire, this proposal uses an expanded Sierra Buttes trail network to connect restoration work across fragmented land ownership in Plumas County. Walking becomes a way to understand recovery and participate in a changing forest landscape.

Around Greenville, routes follow terrain and parcel boundaries, linking areas at different stages of treatment. Logging, vegetation management and replanting become visible along the journey. A recovery calendar explains why repeated intervention matters as fuel builds up over time.

Lookouts, interpretive markers and environmental monitoring connect recreation with forest stewardship. Reused biomass helps protect the ground, while trail corridors support ongoing management. The proposal presents recovery as a shared, long-term responsibility rather than a single completed intervention.
